issues.legal_issue: Regulations made by a statutory housing board under its enabling statute with the required government sanction have statutory force.
material_facts: The housing board was a statutory body created under the governing Act.
The board made regulations under the Act with the previous sanction of the State Government.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to hold that the regulations were not statutory and lacked force as such.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 67(1) of the Bombay Housing Board Act, 1948, the Board could make regulations, with the State Government’s previous sanction, consistent with the Act and rules made under it. The Court relied on Sukhdev Singh v. Bhagat Ram Sardar Singh Raghubanshi for the statutory character of such regulations.

predicates.statutory_housing_board: A statutory housing board was responsible for administering the housing scheme.
predicates.regulations_made_under_enabling_law_with: The board made regulations under its enabling law after obtaining the sanction that law required.

issues.definition: When a statutory housing board makes regulations under its enabling law after obtaining the required sanction, those regulations have statutory force.

issues.legal_issue: A housing board may charge enhanced rent retrospectively from the point when a tenant crosses the applicable income limit if a binding government direction authorizes reduced subsidy or economic rent, subject to the prescribed concession period.
material_facts: The tenants were industrial workers allotted homes at subsidized rents under a housing scheme, subject to family-income limits.
The tenants later exceeded the applicable wage limit.

The tenancy documents described the rent as provisional and required payment of revised rent and charges, though the regulations and documents did not clearly specify the consequence of exceeding the limit.

The State Government directed the Board to reduce the subsidy or charge economic rent when tenants crossed the relevant limits, allowing a three-month concession; the direction was issued under statutory authority.
The Board demanded enhanced rent for periods before the notices were issued, beginning from dates tied to the tenants’ crossing the income limit and the applicable concession period.
issues.conclusion: The State Government had power under section 73A of the Act to direct retrospective charging from the relevant date, after the three-month concession; the Board’s demands were lawful, and the tenants could not insist on continuing at the original subsidized rent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 73A of the Bombay Housing Board Act, 1948 empowered the State Government to give directions necessary or expedient to carry out the Act, and required the Board to comply. Regulations 3, 4, 6 and 7 established the housing classifications, government-set rents and applicable income limits. Although neither the regulations nor the tenancy documents clearly stated the consequences of crossing the limit, the agreement and undertaking contemplated revised charges, and the State’s direction clarified the ambiguity without contradicting them. A tenant who crossed the applicable limit was not entitled to retain the original subsidized rent; the direction could apply from the relevant past date, subject to the three-month concession.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_retrospective_rent_demand and subsidized_industrial_housing_tenancy and tenant_crossed_applicable_income_limit and binding_government_direction_authorizes_rent_adjustment and direction_allows_concession_period

predicates.appeal_challenges_retrospective_rent_dem: The proceeding challenges a demand for increased rent covering a period before the demand notice.
predicates.subsidized_industrial_housing_tenancy: A tenant occupies housing allotted under an industrial-worker scheme at a subsidized rent tied to income eligibility.
predicates.tenant_crossed_applicable_income_limit: The tenant’s income exceeded the limit relevant to continued subsidized rent or eligibility for the applicable rent category.
predicates.binding_government_direction_authorizes_: The government issued a direction under its statutory authority requiring the board to reduce the subsidy or charge a higher rent when the income limit was crossed.
predicates.direction_allows_concession_period: The direction preserves a specified concession period after the tenant crosses the income limit before the increased charge applies.

issues.definition: If a challenge concerns a retrospective rent demand under a subsidized industrial-housing tenancy, the tenant crossed the applicable income limit, and a binding government direction authorizes rent adjustment after a concession period, the retrospective enhanced-rent demand is valid.
